p:Lax496464Proofs.WHierarchy.MccNP.Corre.label:
`G` has an independent set of size at least `k` if and only if its multicoloured graph has a
multicoloured clique: the copies `(c, v_c)` of `k` pairwise different, pairwise non-adjacent
vertices form one, and conversely the vertices of a multicoloured clique are such a family.
p:Lax496464Proofs.WHierarchy.MccNP.Corre.tooltipHtml: GGG has an independent set of size at least kkk if and only if its multicoloured graph has a multicoloured clique: the copies (c,vc)(c, v_c)(c,vc​) of kkk pairwise different, pairwise non-adjacent vertices form one, and conversely the vertices of a multicoloured clique are such a family.

p:Lax496464Proofs.WHierarchy.MccNP.Hardn.label:
Independent Set fpt-reduces to Multicoloured Clique with `g k = (k + 1) ^ 2` and `h k = k`: the map
is correct, sends words of instances to words of instances, preserves the parameter `k`, and runs
in time `c * (k + 1) ^ 2 * (|x| + 1)`.

p:Lax496464Proofs.WHierarchy.MccNP.Param.label:
The parameter is preserved, `k' = k`: the word of an independent-set instance is mapped to the word of
its multicoloured graph, whose last entry is the threshold, which is the parameter of the
independent-set word.

p:Lax496464Proofs.WHierarchy.MccNP.Ram.F.label:
The reduction is computed by one word RAM program, the compilation of the IMP+ program that reads
the word into an array, using its own structure, and then writes the word of the multicoloured
graph: the number of vertices, the number of edges, the offsets, the targets and the colours, each
computed by a pass over all ordered pairs of copies. The program runs within
`c (k + 1)² (|x| + 1)` instructions, and every value it computes is below the value bound that
the fitting conditions on the word and on its image provide.

The program runs within c(k+1)2(∣x∣+1)c (k + 1)² (|x| + 1)c(k+1)2(∣x∣+1) instructions, and every value it computes is below the value bound that the fitting conditions on the word and on its image provide.

p:Lax496464Proofs.WHierarchy.MccNP.Ram.P.label:
The reduction is computed in polynomial time by one word RAM program, the compilation of the IMP+
program that reads the length-prefixed word into an array, decides in one linear pass whether the
word has the shape of an encoding, and, if it does, writes the word of the multicoloured graph
with the passes of the fixed-parameter program; on every other word it writes nothing. The run
costs at most `16300 (bitSize x + 1)^3` instructions when the word length fits the values, all of
which are below `(|x| + 2)^4 + max x + 1`.

p:Lax496464Proofs.WHierarchy.MccNP.Reduc.label:
Yes-instances go to yes-instances and no-instances to no-instances: both sides are the
correctness of the construction.
p:Lax496464Proofs.WHierarchy.MccNP.Reduc.tooltipHtml:
Yes-instances go to yes-instances and no-instances to no-instances: both sides are the
correctness of the construction.

p:Lax496464Proofs.WHierarchy.MccNP.Reduc.label: The image of the word of an instance is the word of the construction, which encodes it.
p:Lax496464Proofs.WHierarchy.MccNP.Reduc.tooltipHtml: The image of the word of an instance is the word of the construction, which encodes it.

p:Lax496464Proofs.WHierarchy.MccNP.Reduc.label: On a word that presents no instance the reduction is the empty word: such a word is not valid.
p:Lax496464Proofs.WHierarchy.MccNP.Reduc.tooltipHtml: On a word that presents no instance the reduction is the empty word: such a word is not valid.

p:Lax496464Proofs.WHierarchy.MccNP.Reduc.label:
On the word of an instance the reduction is the word of the construction: the encoding is
injective, so the instance chosen by the definition is the instance itself.
p:Lax496464Proofs.WHierarchy.MccNP.Reduc.tooltipHtml:
On the word of an instance the reduction is the word of the construction: the encoding is

p:Lax496464Proofs.WHierarchy.MccNP.WordE.label:
**The word encodes the construction.** The word is the compressed sparse row block (the header
`[N, M]`, the prefix sums of the degrees, the concatenated increasing neighbour lists), the
colours `⌊s / n⌋`, and `k`; the block encodes the multicoloured graph, the length of the
target array being even by the degree-sum formula, and each block is strictly increasing.
